pages.text: Buzz-buzz! Bea the bee zips out of the hive, searching for bright flowers like tiny treasure cups.
Bea is an insect with six legs. She uses her wings to fly and her antennae to smell.
A sweet smell leads Bea to a bloom. She sips nectar, the sugary liquid flowers make.
Yellow pollen dust sticks to Bea’s fuzzy body. Pollen is like plant ‘powder’ that helps plants make seeds.
Next flower! As Bea visits, she carries pollen between blossoms. This is pollination, and it helps plants grow fruit.
Bea flies home to her colony. A honey bee home is a hive, full of busy workers and one queen.
Inside, Bea does a waggle dance. Her moves tell friends where the best flowers are.
Workers share nectar and turn it into honey. Honey is stored in waxy honeycomb cells.
Bea rests, then buzzes out again. Helping flowers helps gardens, farms, and many foods we eat.
Bedtime fact: bees are tiny helpers. They pollinate flowers and keep their hive working together like a team.
